title: Property tests pin the dashboard layout invariants
description:
Epic hn6, wave 4: property tests for the dashboard layout, run in the per-tick gate (Go, stdlib only, headless). This is the in-gate half of acceptance A6. The Bombadil TUI half is tick z7w's (a separate task outside this epic), and those properties target this same layout.

The renderer under test is `renderWatchFrame(m statusmodel.Model, st watchStyles, width, height int, selected string) []string` in internal/cli/watch_view.go. It is a pure function. Use the identity style set the existing tests in internal/cli/watch_view_test.go use.

Build internal/cli/watch_props_test.go:
- A seeded generator, `genModel(r *rand.Rand) statusmodel.Model`, using math/rand/v2 with a fixed seed list plus the `-seed` flag. It produces 1–6 waves of 1–8 ticks with random states. Pipelines are consistent with those states (use statusmodel.PipelineImplement / PipelineReview / PipelineCloseout). Some ticks get parent_tick_id pointing at an earlier tick. It also draws 0–3 attention entries (some needs_person with an unblock_command), 0–3 workers with activity, cost lines mixing metered and unmetered, and 0–5 recent events. It also has `advance(m, r)`, which moves some ticks forward (ready→dispatched→closed) WITHOUT changing the graph's order.
- Run each property over 500 generated models, at widths drawn from {0, 30, 47, 63, 80, 99, 120, 200} and heights from {0, 8, 12, 24, 60}:
  P1 rows never reorder: the tick ids, in the order their rows appear in frame(m), are a subsequence of plan order. For frame(advance(m)), the order of the ids visible in both frames is unchanged.
  P2 needs-you is never empty while a hold exists: if any attention has needs_person, then some line contains "needs you:" plus that attention's unblock command (when it has one) and no line says "needs you: nothing". Otherwise "needs you: nothing" appears (at height 0 or ≥ 8).
  P3 never $0.00 for unmetered spend: when any cost line is unmetered, "$0.00" never appears on the cost line, and "not metered" does.
  P4 the frame fits the pane: when width > 0, every line's ansi.StringWidth ≤ width; when height > 0, len(frame) ≤ height.
- Non-vacuity, proven in the gate: each property is a func(frame, model) error. TestDashboardPropertiesCatchSeededBugs runs each property against a deliberately broken renderer and requires the property to FAIL for at least one generated model. The four broken renderers: a wrapper that reverses the table rows (P1), one that drops the attention lines (P2), one that replaces "not metered" with "$0.00" (P3), and one that pads the first line by 5 columns (P4).
- On failure, print the seed and the minimal failing model as JSON.
- The "first frame within its bound" property is NOT here: it is a wall-clock property, and it stays with internal/cli/status_firstframe_test.go and z7w. Say so in a comment.

Files: new internal/cli/watch_props_test.go. If a property finds a REAL renderer bug, make the smallest fix in internal/cli/watch_view.go. No other tick in this wave edits that file. Name each bug found in your report: the report of what the properties found is part of the deliverable.

Tests: TestDashboardProperties and TestDashboardPropertiesCatchSeededBugs. Keep the total runtime under 5s, because it runs in the gate.

Run: `go test -short -timeout 20m -run 'TestDashboardProperties' ./internal/cli/`. Must still pass: `go test -short -timeout 20m ./internal/cli/`, and then `make gate`.
